OK, I will update the PR to fix them together.

Hi @DaveCTurner , I have updated the PR. Here are the related logics:

If cluster has read only blocks and archived settings:
1. Cannot remove read only blocks due to archived settings.
2. Cannot update any cluster settings due to read only blocks.
3. Can only remove archived settings.

That means we cannot do any changes before removing archived settings. And if cluster is read only, except removing archived settings, we could do nothing include removing read only blocks.

Now we also support removing transient and persistent cluster blocks together.

issue_context.title: Cluster read only settings and archived settings conflict issue.
comments: @howardhuanghua I'm not sure if it will work, but have you tried deleting the archived settings in the same request as clearing the cluster block?
Hi @rjernst, would you please help to review the issue again? Could I open a PR to fix the issue with my proposal?

@howardhuanghua I don't think we would want such a flag. We always want validation. This is an edge case, but I'm hopeful we can find another solution. I've reached out to some other folks to solicit additional thoughts.

@rjernst thanks. Yes, this is an edge case, but if user got this case, it would be fatal, user cannot recover the cluster anymore. It's my pleasure to fix this issue if you could advise some better solutions.

You can recover from this in more recent versions using [`elasticsearch-node remove-settings`](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/node-tool.html#_removing_persistent_cluster_settings) although that's not ideal.

I think it would be reasonable to allow removing the block and the archived settings in a single call. I don't think we should allow the two-step process proposed above since it completely bypasses some of the validation that we have in place today.

@DaveCTurner thanks for the suggestion. As far as I know, `archived` settings are coming from the duplicated settings during upgrading the cluster? User cannot set any `archived.*` settings? So the only case we set `archived.*` settings is to clean them? I mean user doesn't have any chance to set `archived.*` settings, so we could skip validation in `AbstractScopedSettings`?

If we still need to keep this validation, then check both cluster blocking status setting and `archived.*` settings together during validation, skip validation if both of them existing in the settings list? I am not sure user could get this point or not, we didn’t expect to set them at the same time before **rjernst**'s suggestion.

I think I don't fully understand your proposed changes to the validation. You seem to be suggesting skipping all validation of archived settings, which is definitely unacceptable: it's deliberate that you cannot do anything in the cluster until you clear the archived settings to acknowledge that they are no longer in force. You also cannot do anything in the cluster until you remove any read-only blocks. This is why it makes sense to me to try and do both of these in a single call. It is fair to say that this isn't clear from the docs, and we can address that too.

If that's not what you are proposing, then maybe it's simplest to open a PR to show your idea rather than trying to describe it further in words.
